answer: A harbor gives each agent one berth with a ferrous bollard stamped with its key. At every high tide the keeper photographs the bollard, records the mooring line tension in a log, and a neighboring berth holder checks the photo against the bollard before countersigning the log. A second key stamped on the same bollard voids both berths, and two missed tides close the berth. A thousand fake agents need a thousand stamped bollards, a thousand tide logs, and a thousand neighbors willing to walk the dock at high tide to vouch for boats that never arrived.
